subject: general
question: Who is the author of the novel 'A Suitable Boy' which is one of the longest novels?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikram Seth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"A Suitable Boy," **penned by **Vikram Seth** and released in 1993, stands as one of the** lengthiest novels published in a single volume**, boasting **1,349 pages** (1,488 pages in paperback) in its English edition.
 
• This narrative unfolds against the backdrop of post-independence, post-partition India, intricately woven across 19 parts, each delving into a distinct subplot.
 
• Vikram Seth, an acclaimed Indian novelist and poet, has authored numerous novels and poetry collections.
 
• His literary prowess has garnered him prestigious accolades, including** the Padma Shri, Sahitya Academy Award, Pravasi Bharatiya Samman, WH Smith Literary Award, and Crossword Book Award.**
 
• Seth's contributions to Indian English language poetry, particularly through works like "Mappings" and "Beastly Tales," have left a lasting imprint on the literary landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rohinton Mistry, **an Indian-born Canadian author, has garnered numerous accolades throughout his career, including the prestigious Neustadt International Prize for Literature in 2012.
 
• **R.K. Narayan,** hailed as one of the preeminent Indian authors of the twentieth century, was born in 1906. His contributions to literature earned him the National Prize of the Indian Literary Academy, India's foremost literary distinction.
 
• **Salman Rushdie**, an Indian-born British-American novelist, is renowned for his unique blend of magic realism and historical fiction. His works often explore the interplay between Eastern and Western civilizations, with a particular focus on the Indian subcontinent, addressing themes of connection, disruption, and migration.
